mission: Final image — Ben walks the Temple corridors. The Force hums differently now. The new seal's resonance is part of his perception — a note in a chord. He's at peace with his name. Not because he's earned it, but because he's redefined what it means.
why_now: The novel's closing beat — the emotional and thematic resolution in a single image
conflict: None — this is resolution. The conflict is behind him. What remains is the new equilibrium: a Ben Skywalker who knows the truth, carries the resonance, and has learned that leadership is orchestration, not possession.
turning_point: The final sensory callback: the wrongness from Chapter 1 is gone. In its place, the resonance — the three-part harmony of the new seal humming at the edge of perception. A note he's part of. A chord he helped build. Not enough by itself. Enough as part of something larger.
opening_hook: The Temple corridors in evening light. The same walk he took in Chapter 1, when the wrongness was everything he could hear and no one else would listen.
closing_hook: A note in a chord. Enough.
emotional_trajectory: Reflective peace -> the new perception -> acceptance and forward motion

stakes.personal: Ben's relationship with his legacy — at peace, redefined
stakes.interpersonal: His place in the Order — changed, honest, ongoing
stakes.external: The new seal humming, the truth told, the work continuing

setting: Jedi Temple, Coruscant — corridors, evening light, the same walk as Chapter 1
sensory_details: Evening light through Temple windows; the corridor's familiar Force harmonics — warmer now, or maybe Ben is warmer; the resonance humming at the edge of perception — not wrongness but harmony; his footsteps steady, unhurried; the future open
promises_paid: Ben finds a new relationship with his legacy (PP21)
Ben's unique Force perception resolves into his own frequency (PP22)
notes: Final image: 'A note in a chord. Enough.' Deliberate sensory callback to the opening wrongness. The wrongness became understanding became harmony. Ben's arc complete. The book ends not with triumph but with belonging.
